evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a self-contained feature; it does not explicitly require another story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: give them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by giving a game URL inherently requires a game to exist (creation of the game).

evaluations.evidence: start a round
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game session to start the round in, so it depends on game creation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the session's items can be implemented independently; it does not explicitly require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to estimate inherently requires that items exist (i.e., an ability to add/import items), which is provided by the add-item story.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items must target a specific game session, so it inherently depends on the ability to create a game.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item presupposes items exist (added or imported); it therefore depends on the add-item story.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires items to exist (added/imported), so it depends on the add-item capability.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates immediately is a display policy; it does not explicitly require another backlog story to be implemented first (no concrete requirement-level dependency stated).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average is a standalone moderator action; it does not explicitly reference or require another specific story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatically filling the estimate when all estimators have shown cards depends on the system being able to detect that all estimates have been given/shown (the feature for revealing all estimates after everyone has voted).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering the agreed-upon estimate is a standalone moderator action and does not explicitly require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a story requires selecting that prior story as the current item, so it depends on the select-item (or item-management) story.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories must place them into a game/session, so it inherently depends on the ability to have/create a game.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories is an input mechanism that targets a game/session, so it depends on game creation being available.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires that games have been created and stored, so it depends on the game-creation/persistence capability.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript requires that the game and its stories/estimates have been recorded, which depends on game creation/storage.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript presupposes the transcript feature is available (viewing/storing transcripts), so it depends on the transcript story.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript to CSV requires that transcripts are stored/viewable; it therefore depends on the transcript story.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presumes games exist to be deleted, so it depends on the ability to create/store games.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a standalone feature and does not inherently depend on any other backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires the existence of an account, so it depends on the account-creation story.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presupposes a user account exists; it therefore depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires that an account exists; it depends on the account-creation story.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying times in local timezone is a standalone presentation requirement and does not explicitly depend on other backlog items.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders presuppose user accounts and authentication data exist; this depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting the estimation scale is a configuration option and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators is an extension of the invitation capability and thus depends on the invitation (URL) feature.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL explicitly depends on the existence of the invitation URL feature.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: To see the current item being estimated, there must be a mechanism that sets the current item (starting a round/selecting an item), so it depends on the start-round story.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Estimator viewing of the session item list depends on the moderator/item-list capability to present and store those items.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This presence/indicator UI requirement can be implemented on its own and does not explicitly cite another backlog story as a prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates simultaneously is a display rule; it can be implemented standalone without an explicit dependency on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Allowing estimate changes during a draw is a self-contained interaction rule and does not explicitly require another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Displaying prior estimates can be implemented as a discrete feature and does not explicitly require a different backlog story, though it may use stored data.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying per-estimator current-round estimates is a standalone display requirement and does not cite another explicit prerequisite story.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer feature is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting the timer when everyone has played requires detection that all estimates have been given, which is the responsibility of the 'all estimates given / reveal' functionality.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back through prior rounds presupposes that prior round data (transcripts/history) is stored and available, which depends on the transcript/history feature.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining a consistent card order is an independent UI requirement and does not explicitly require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: This behaviour constraint is a standalone interaction rule and does not explicitly reference another prerequisite story.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a UI feature; while it may use profile data, the story itself does not explicitly depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a non-dependent developer task and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is a self-contained documentation feature and does not explicitly depend on other backlog items.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Index creation is a developer task that does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a quality requirement and not explicitly dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is an independent quality goal and does not explicitly require another story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance/responsiveness is a non-dependent quality requirement and does not explicitly require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a standalone technical requirement and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is an independent usability requirement and does not explicitly reference another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages are a standalone UI/UX feature and do not inherently depend on a different backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Research storage of results presupposes that game results (stories and estimates) are stored/retrievable (transcript/history capability).

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics is a reporting feature; while it uses collected data, the story does not explicitly cite a specific backlog story dependency.
